chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rib'i ibn Abdillah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever emancipates a Muslim, Allah Mighty and Majestic will emancipate him for every organ of his — an organ from the Fire.'

key_terms.أَعْتَقَ: emancipated / freed (a slave); root ع-ت-ق, related to the concept of nobility and freedom
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — a standard honorific for Allah

ai.seo_question: What reward does Islam promise for freeing a Muslim slave?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (saww) promises a remarkable divine recompense for the act of freeing a Muslim slave: for every bodily organ of the emancipated person, Allah will spare the liberator a corresponding organ from hellfire. This hadith was transmitted by Imam al-Baqir (AS) and reached Kulayni through a chain including the eminent Zurara ibn A'yan and Ibn Abi Umayr. In the context of early Islamic society, where slavery was an established institution, this teaching provided powerful incentive for manumission, framing it as an act of profound spiritual and eschatological consequence.
